introduction: On this Sunday, the first reading takes us back to the garden, where God calls to Adam, Where are you? and promises that the serpent's head will be crushed. In the Gospel, Jesus is accused of being in league with Satan, and he declares that those who do God's will are his brother, sister and mother. Paul assures us that our inner self is renewed day by day. Let us come out of hiding and stand before the Lord.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, with the Lord there is mercy and fullness of redemption. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be a family of brothers and sisters who do the will of God together. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who live in fear or shame: that they may hear God's voice calling them out of hiding and into his mercy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families divided by misunderstanding or conflict: that they may find healing and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick and the elderly, whose bodies are weakening: that their inner self may be renewed day by day. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may not lose heart, but fix our eyes on what is eternal. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Merciful Father, you sought us out when we hid from you, and you promised a Savior. Make us members of your family who do your will. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Where are you?
reflection.body:
The first question God asks in the Bible after the fall is not an accusation. It is a call: "Where are you?" Adam answers honestly about his fear: "I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself." Then comes the blame: the man blames the woman, the woman blames the serpent. Sin isolates us and makes us hide, from God and from one another.

Yet even here God speaks of hope. To the serpent he says, "I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head." The Church has long seen in these words the first promise of a Savior.

The psalm answers with confidence: "If you, LORD, kept a record of sins, Lord, who could stand? But there is forgiveness with you."

In the Gospel, Jesus faces misunderstanding from two sides. His own relatives think he is out of his mind, and the scribes say he casts out demons by the power of demons. Jesus answers that Satan cannot drive out Satan: "If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand." Christ has come to bind the strong man and set his captives free.

Then he looks around at those sitting in the circle with him and says, "Behold, my mother and my brothers! For whoever does the will of God is my brother, my sister, and mother." Mary is, of course, the first of those who do God's will. And all of us are invited into that family.

Paul adds a word of comfort for anyone growing older or weaker: "though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day." This week, answer God's question honestly in prayer: where am I? Then let him find you.
